title: Complementary Filter Heading Tuner
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A compass dial shows four needles at once: the true heading, a drifting gyro-only estimate, a jittery magnetometer-only estimate, and the fused complementary-filter estimate from the chapter's HeadingFilter code. Students move the alpha slider and read live and 5-second-average errors to see which sensor the fused estimate trusts.

educational.topic: Complementary filter sensor fusion for heading estimation
learningObjectives: Compare gyro-only, magnetometer-only, and fused heading estimates against a true heading.
Explain why an integrated gyroscope heading drifts and a magnetometer heading jitters.
Attribute fused-estimate drift to an alpha that is too high and jitter to an alpha that is too low.
Predict how the best alpha changes when gyro drift or magnetometer noise changes.
standards: NGSS HS-ETS1-3: Evaluate a solution to a complex real-world problem based on prioritized criteria and trade-offs.

controls.label: Start Turn
controls.purpose: Turn the true heading 90 degrees over 2 seconds, then hold.

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Restore defaults, zero all estimates, and clear the chart.

equations: gyro_z = true turn rate + drift + noise
compass = true heading + Gaussian noise (standard deviation = Mag noise)
fused = alpha * (fused + gyro_z * dt) + (1 - alpha) * compass, with the compass difference measured the short way around the circle
assumptions: The magnetometer is already hard-iron calibrated, so it has noise but no offset.
dt = 0.02 s, matching the build plan's 50 Hz loop.
limitations: Tilt, magnetic disturbances from motors, and gyro scale-factor error are not modeled.
The true heading is known to the simulation only, never to the robot.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Simultaneous comparison against ground truth with quantified error
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Live four-needle dial, error table with 5-second averages, and a strip chart, driven by parameter sliders
keyQuestions: Which estimate drifts, which jitters, and which stays closest to the truth?
What happens to the fused needle when alpha is 0.999? When it is 0.80?
Why does the best alpha drop when the gyroscope drifts more?
commonMisconceptions: The magnetometer alone is good enough because it never drifts.
A higher alpha is always better because it trusts the smooth sensor more.
The fused estimate is an equal 50/50 average of the two sensors.
assessmentOpportunities: Alpha sweep table and U-shaped error sketch.
Predict the best alpha for high drift and for high noise, then test.
Exit ticket: diagnose a fused heading that creeps while the robot is still.
